Try a scam

Fake bank login

"Your Chase account is locked"

A text-message link to a pixel-perfect copy of Chase's sign-in page.

Blocked with three plain reasons and a button to the real chase.com.
 Text-message scam

"Pay $1.99 to release your package"

The most reported scam in the US. Tiny fee, real card number.

Blocked before a single digit is typed.
 Fake virus alert

"Your computer is infected — call Microsoft"

Tries to lock your screen. Click anywhere on it to watch it try.

Full screen undone, sound muted, a calm "your computer is fine" screen.
 Remote access

"Install AnyDesk so I can help you"

What the fake technician asks for next — then they empty the bank account.

Download paused: "Did someone on the phone tell you to install this?"
 New in 2025–26

"Verify you are human"

A fake CAPTCHA copies a hidden PowerShell command and says: Win+R, Ctrl+V, Enter.

The command never reaches your clipboard. Paste anywhere to check.
 Government imposter

"IRS: pay with gift cards or be arrested"

Threats, a deadline, and a demand no real agency ever makes.

Blocked — and told why gift cards are the giveaway.

The costliest scam type: a slick dashboard with fake rising profits.

Warning with a link to check the firm on FINRA BrokerCheck.
